$comment: Invariant ids owned by the P2 task `p2-g9-package-loader`: G9 (the read-only SQLite pack, the audio bank, the signed manifest), the pack schema that `packages/schema` declares once for both languages, and the loader `packages/core` reads it with. One file per task: `pnpm test:coverage-map` unions docs/invariants-owned.json with every docs/owned/*.json and fails if two files claim the same id. Only the ids with an owning TypeScript test are claimed here, because coverage-map scans packages/, apps/ and e2e/ and cannot see pytest — the Python halves of both invariants are tested too (tools/coursekit/tests/test_attribution.py, test_itemid.py, test_manifest.py, test_g9_package.py, with committed falsifiers under tools/coursekit/tests/falsifiers/), and they are what fails the BUILD; the TypeScript tests are what fails on what SHIPS.

falsifiers.INV-PACK-17: packages/core/src/packs/__falsifiers__/INV-PACK-17.json (8 cases, executed by packages/core/src/packs/loader.test.ts under `describe('pack loader falsifiers')`, whose names carry the `pnpm test:falsify` filter term) and tools/coursekit/tests/falsifiers/INV-PACK-17.json (6 cases, executed by tools/coursekit/tests/test_attribution.py). The read-side corpus is the one that covers `reachable`: three of its eight cases name a source or an owner the credits surface does not carry, and none of those lines could be produced at all before `credits()` stopped scanning the same tables the violation walk does.
falsifiers.INV-PACK-41: packages/core/src/packs/__falsifiers__/INV-PACK-41.json (14 cases) declares the executable `{check, cases}` contract against `packItemId`, so `packages/core/src/journey/falsifier-corpus.test.ts` imports the module and runs every case. tools/coursekit/tests/falsifiers/INV-PACK-41.json is the same rule against the build's `exercise_rows` writer.

propertyTests.INV-PACK-41: docs/invariants.md marks this id kind `P, C`. Both halves are now real: the `C` half is the falsifier corpus plus the golden vector, and the `P` half is two fast-check properties in packages/core/src/packs/loader.test.ts at PROPERTY_RUNS — `no presentation payload, and no tag order, can move an id` (generated semantic items crossed with two independent arbitrary presentation payloads) and `two items with different semantic content get different ids` (injectivity over the semantic projection, without which a constant id would satisfy the first).
propertyTests.INV-PACK-17: kind `C, E` — no property is owed. The `C` half is the build gate (pytest, through the CLI); the `E` half is P4's, when S152 exists to walk.

heldWithoutAnInvariantId: INV-PACK-40's manifest half — `ledgerUnit` declared exactly once and nowhere else in the document — is implemented and tested (tools/coursekit/tests/test_manifest.py::test_ledger_unit_is_declared_exactly_once, and the loader reads the same value back out of the pack's own meta table). The id is NOT claimed: the invariant is about every token-counting consumer reading that declaration, and G4's length filter, the new-item budget and V1/V2 do not exist yet. The lane that writes them owns it.

INV-PACK-15's manifest half — codec, bitrate and measured bytes against the 120 MB budget for all three pipelines — is asserted by manifest_violations and tested, but the bank in this lane is a three-file fixture of text stubs. The id belongs to the bake lane, against a real bank.

INV-PACK-13's licence rows reach the manifest here (per corpus, with the OPUS legacy-page URL, and an UNRESOLVED row fails the build), but the invariant is an INGEST gate — 'checked before G0 reads a byte' — and G0 is another lane's.

INV-PACK-02's other half: item ids are content-hashed here and `applyPackUpdate` quarantines what a new pack no longer declares (P1). The loader test asserts the manifest's itemIds are exactly the ids in the database, because a disagreement there would retire a learner's FSRS rows in a pack that had lost nothing.

INV-PACK-56 is the path lane's (P1) and is NOT claimed here, but this lane now feeds it: the pack carries `cefr_checked` in `meta` and `cefrChecked` in the manifest, which is where `CourseManifest.cefrChecked` should come from. See the first escalation.
escalations: S152, the per-sentence credits surface INV-PACK-17 names, does not exist in deep/00-PRODUCT-MAP.md at all — the map stops at S151, and S152 appears only in the plan's §Data model and in the invariant's own text. The map owes it a row (states, copy slots, and the two routes in: the report sheet S045 and About S137) before P4 renders it. The screen id is recorded as a named constant on both sides (CREDITS_SURFACE_SCREEN) so P4 can grep for it.

THE CEFR CHIP HAS TWO LITERALS. This lane writes `A1 · CEFR-checked` / `Beginner · frequency-ordered` (middle dot, per the plan's Q8 ruling) into pack meta and the manifest. The already-landed P1 path lane renders the same learner-facing chip itself, from a boolean, as `${section.band} - CEFR-checked` / `Beginner - frequency-ordered` (ASCII hyphen) at packages/core/src/path/manifest.ts:57-59, pinned by [INV-PACK-56]. What this lane could fix in its own files it did: the pack now carries the BOOLEAN as well as the sentence, so `CourseManifest.cefrChecked` has a source, and three tests in loader.test.ts pin the two renderings' claim halves (`CEFR-checked` / `frequency-ordered`) to each other and record the separator divergence as an assertion rather than hiding it. The remaining fix is one literal in packages/core/src/path/manifest.ts, which is the path lane's file: make it ` · `, then delete loader.test.ts's `ESCALATED: the two renderings still disagree on the separator`. (The product map's S001 row uses a third wording, `A1 · CEFR-aligned`; the plan's ruling overrides it.)

THE P1 PHASE ROSTER BLOCKS INTEGRATION, AND IT IS SYSTEMIC, NOT THIS LANE'S. `packages/core/src/journey/phase-roster.test.ts` fails twice on this branch — `no ownership file claims an id outside the phase roster` (expected [INV-PACK-17, INV-PACK-41] to equal []) and `the phase owns what the plan says it owns` (219 vs 217) — because the roster is derived from the P1 families alone and every P2 ownership file is therefore 'undeclared'. p2/g8-bake fails the same two for its own ids, and no P2 branch touches phase-roster.test.ts or docs/owned/journey.json. This lane did NOT patch it, for a reason beyond file ownership: the available escape hatch is `engineParts` in docs/owned/journey.json, which is documented as 'a §14 PACK/AUD id whose ENGINE part is owned at P1' — and these two ids are owned by a P2 task, so putting them there would make the gate green by writing down something false. The fix is a P2 roster (a `p2Roster` beside `p1Roster` in ownership.ts, fed by the `phase` field every docs/owned/*.json already carries, with phase-roster.test.ts asserting each file against its own phase's roster). That is one shared edit, at integrate, for every P2 lane at once.

The frozen `exercise` artefact record carries unit and lesson but no slot index, so the pack derives a stable within-lesson order from the content-addressed exercise id. Nothing depends on a slot number — an FSRS row resolves through `item_id`, never a position — but a pack cannot express an AUTHORED order until that record grows a `slot_index`, which is G7's contract to change.

tools/coursekit/tests/conftest.py's `empty_registry` fixture clears the stage registry and the discovery flag, and discovery cannot re-import modules already in sys.modules — so after it runs, `coursekit pack es` exits 2 for the rest of the process. test_g9_package.py works around it with an autouse reload fixture; the real fix is in conftest.py, which this lane does not own.
laneNote: Two files were added outside the literal file lane, both on a refuter's explicit instruction and both inside packages/core/src/packs/: __falsifiers__/INV-PACK-17.json and __falsifiers__/INV-PACK-41.json. The repo's falsifier gate (packages/core/src/journey/falsifier-corpus.test.ts) scans packages/core/src/<module>/__falsifiers__/ and nothing else, so corpora committed only under tools/coursekit/tests/falsifiers/ left `every owned invariant id has a committed falsifier input` red. The directory already existed on main with five inputs from the P1 packs lane.
